source_text:
2 Πῶς ἐγκωμιάσω τὸν τοῦ Χριστοῦ
δοῦλον καὶ ἀδελφόν, τὸν τῆς νέας Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἀρχιστράτηγον, τὸν τῶν ἱερέων
ἡγεμόνα, τῶν ἀποστόλων τὸν ἔξαρχον, τὸν ἐν κεφαλαῖς κορυφήν, τὸν ἐν λύχνοις
ὑπερλάμποντα, τὸν ἐν ἄστροις ὑπερφαίνοντα; Πέτρος δημηγορεῖ, ἀλλ' Ἰάκωβος
νομοθετεῖ, καὶ ὀλίγαι λέξεις τὸ τοῦ ζητήματος συνέστειλαν μέγεθος· «Ἐγὼ κρίνω μὴ
παρενοχλεῖν τοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν, καὶ ἑξῆς».
thought_title: How to praise James, the servant and brother of Christ
orientation: Hesychius, the preacher, is asking how he can worthily praise James, the brother of the Lord, after contrasting Bethlehem and Zion.
pass_a_gloss: How [shall I] praise the [one] of Christ slave and brother, the [one] of the new Jerusalem commander-in-chief, the [one] of the priests leader, of the apostles the chief, the [one] in heads summit, the [one] in lamps shining-beyond, the [one] in stars appearing-beyond? Peter speaks-publicly, but James legislates, and few words the of the question restrained magnitude; "I judge not to trouble the [ones] from the nations, and next."

choices.why: Literal rendering of κορυφή as crown/top, preserving the metaphor of James as the highest point among heads.

choices.english: the one shining beyond among lamps
choices.why: Keeps the comparative force of ὑπερ- and the literal 'lamps' to preserve the image of James outshining other lights.
rejected: the one who outshines the lamps

choices.english: the one appearing beyond among stars
choices.why: Literal rendering of ὑπερφαίνω as appearing beyond, keeping the parallel with the previous clause and the star imagery.
rejected: the one who shines above the stars

choices.term: ὀλίγαι λέξεις τὸ τοῦ ζητήματος συνέστειλαν μέγεθος
choices.english: a few words contracted the magnitude of the question
choices.why: Literal rendering of συνέστειλαν as contracted, preserving the metaphor of reducing the size of the issue.
rejected: a few words settled the great question
a few words brought the great question to a close

choices.term: Ἐγὼ κρίνω μὴ παρενοχλεῖν τοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν
choices.english: I judge not to trouble those from the nations
choices.why: Literal rendering of κρίνω as 'I judge' per glossary, and παρενοχλεῖν as 'to trouble', keeping the infinitive construction.
rejected: I decide not to trouble the Gentiles
I rule that we should not trouble the Gentiles

bible_refs.note: Ἐγὼ κρίνω μὴ παρενοχλεῖν τοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν

pass_b_english: How shall I praise the servant and brother of Christ, the commander-in-chief of the new Jerusalem, the leader of the priests, the chief of the apostles, the crown among heads, the one shining beyond among lamps, the one shining beyond among stars? Peter speaks in public, but James gives the law, and a few words contracted the magnitude of the question: “I judge not to trouble those from the nations,” and so on (Acts 15:19).

problems.quote: the one appearing beyond among stars
problems.why: ὑπερφαίνοντα means shining/brightening beyond, not 'appearing beyond'
problems.fix: the one outshining all other stars
problems.ruling: ὑπερφαίνοντα from φαίνω means 'shining/brightening beyond,' not merely 'appearing beyond'; parallel with ὑπερλάμποντα confirms.

edits.old: the one appearing beyond among stars
edits.new: the one shining beyond among stars

fixed: Changed 'appearing beyond' to 'shining beyond' for ὑπερφαίνοντα, which means shining/brightening beyond, not appearing beyond.

last_rejected.why: "Contracted" suggests shrank/tightened; συνέστειλαν here means "settled" or "resolved" the magnitude of the dispute.
last_rejected.fix: and a few words settled the magnitude of the question
last_rejected.ruling: συνέστειλαν can mean 'contracted/summarized'; rendering within normal range, not a clear error.

last_rejected.source_quote: «Ἐγὼ κρίνω μὴ παρενοχλεῖν τοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν, καὶ ἑξῆς»
last_rejected.why: The quotation matches Acts 15:19, but the citation format should be checked: the source has "I judge" (Ἐγὼ κρίνω) which is Acts 15:19, but the Greek adds καὶ ἑξῆς ("and so on"). The citation is essentially correct, though the Greek form differs slightly from standard critical texts.
last_rejected.ruling: Citation Acts 15:19 is correct for Ἐγὼ κρίνω; καὶ ἑξῆς means 'and so on', accurately translated.
